ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash used in operating activities was $6,045,692 and $126,190 for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The increase of $5,919,502 was driven by two principal factors.

First, our cash operating costs grew substantially faster than gross profit. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $2,407,364 and research and development expenses increased $1,253,963, while gross profit increased only $64,077. The costs driving that growth, principally personnel costs and costs associated with operating as a public company, were substantially settled in cash during the period.

Second, changes in operating assets and liabilities used $3.0 million of cash during the 2026 period, compared to $0.5 million during the 2025 period. The most significant movement was a $1.5 million increase in accounts receivable, with one customer representing 47% of our accounts receivable balance at June 30, 2026. Revenue recognized during the second quarter of 2026 under the research and development contract described above substantially exceeded cash collected under that contract during the period. Accordingly, the improvement in gross profit for the quarter was not accompanied by a corresponding increase in operating cash flow.

gp.text:
Gross profit increased by $3.0 million, or 71%, to $7.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, and gross margin increased to 90% from 79%. The improvement reflects a revenue mix weighted toward software licenses, which carry minimal incremental cost of sales, including the ROC ABIS license delivered during the quarter. Cost of sales decreased by $0.3 million, or 29%, primarily reflecting lower ROC Watch revenue, which carried associated hardware and service delivery costs in the prior-year period, partially offset by $0.2 million of amortization of capitalized software development costs, which began in 2026.

ocf.text: Changes in operating assets and liabilities used $7.9 million of cash during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.1 million during the 2025 period. The most significant driver was a $6.7 million increase in accounts receivable, compared to a $2.6 million increase in the prior-year period. The increase in accounts receivable primarily reflects higher revenue, which was $8.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $5.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, and includes increases in both amounts invoiced under customary payment terms that were not yet due as of quarter-end and contract assets, which represented a significant portion of the increase. Contract assets, which are included in accounts receivable, net, increased to $4.8 million as of September 30, 2026 from $1.2 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily reflecting revenue recognized under research and development contracts and, to a lesser extent, software licenses delivered, for which invoicing occurs in subsequent periods in accordance with contractual milestone and billing schedules. Contract assets generally convert to cash over a longer period than billed receivables because they must first be invoiced and then collected. We expect substantially all contract assets as of September 30, 2026 to be invoiced within the next twelve months.

intro.text: ROC is an independent American artificial intelligence (“AI”) company redefining the global standard for Vision AI in identity, security, and digital forensics. Our Vision AI platform delivers real-time facial recognition, multimodal biometric verification, video analytics, and AI-powered evidence analysis to mission-critical organizations across private and public sectors. ROC’s biometric algorithms are routinely ranked by National Institute of Standards and Technology (“NIST”) as among the most accurate and computationally efficient globally. Our solutions outperform legacy foreign-built systems at a fraction of the cost, with faster deployment and stronger trust. As demand for trusted AI accelerates across law enforcement, defense, and regulated commercial sectors, ROC is scaling rapidly through a growing network of integrators and multi-year deals.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
